rv.q: An exceptionally good show is now on stage at Chicago’s Trap Door Theatre.
It is well-acted and staged, with the clarity and humor of a good folk tale.
It’s amusing and delightfully weird because it’s being staged by Trap Door Theatre, directed by Kay Martinovich.
The Man Who Fell with the Rain isn’t a bad play, but it isn’t a good one either.
This valiant effort to put the story on a stage only underscores how, sometimes, the written word should just stay on the page.
I did enjoy the show’s humor and the thought experiment of how people respond to something miraculous when no further information is forthcoming.
Its uneven pacing may keep the production from fully taking flight, but the mystery surrounding the Old Man and the townspeople’s reactions provide plenty for audiences to contemplate.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this U.S. premiere adaptation of García Márquez's magical realism tale, with some praising its powerful simplicity and humor while others find it hampered by uneven pacing and underdeveloped characters.
